content: For cancer registries, an important piece of information in a pathology report is the associated ICD-O code which describes the patient's histological diagnosis, as described by the World Health Organization's (WHO) International Classification of Diseases for Oncology BIBREF2 . Prediction of the primary diagnosis from a pathology report provides a valuable starting point for exploration of machine learning techniques for automated cancer surveillance. A major application for this purpose would be “auto-reporting” based on analysis of whole slide images, the digitization of the biopsy glass slides. Structured, summarized and categorized reports can be associated with the image content when searching in large archives. Such as system would be able to drastically increase the efficiency of diagnostic processes for the majority of cases where in spite of obvious primary diagnosis, still time and effort is required from the pathologists to write a descriptive report.
